summary: The Baltic Exchange’s dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, fell by 1.3% to 2,980 points on Friday, bringing a seven-day winning streak to an end. The capesize index, which typically transports 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, dropped by 2.4% to 4,719 points, likely tracking lower iron ore prices amid rising supply and weakening demand. Meanwhile, the panamax index, which usually carries 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, rose by 0.1% to a fresh high since October 22 at 2,118 points.
source: Trading Economics public page summarising Baltic Exchange data
